item.title: Sensitivity Analysis for Linear Estimators
item.opening: We propose a framework for building sensitivity analyses for linear estimators. We measure the degree of identification failure by the change of measure between the observed distribution and a hypothetical target distribution under which a standard estimator would identify the parameter of interest. Under L_infinity bounds on that derivative, the identified set has closed-form sharp bounds that require no numerical optimization and that are computable and continuous when the derivative is unbounded, nesting Manski-type worst-case bounds and existing characterizations that require bounded changes of measure. The framework nests several selection models for average potential outcomes, yielding the established worst-case bounds of each design. The framework yields a new model family for regression discontinuity (RD) that delivers the first sensitivity analysis on the conditional average treatment effect under manipulation. We show that a bootstrap procedure yields valid confidence intervals. An empirical application shows that a modest restriction on manipulation delivers bounds far more informative than worst-case bounds.
